name: Naltrexone

track.title: Lab & animal
track.line: Opioid blocker; with bupropion acts on appetite cells

what.text: Naltrexone is an opioid antagonist: it blocks the brain's opioid receptors. Alone, it is approved for alcohol dependence and to block the effects of opioids after detox. For weight, it is approved only in one tablet with bupropion, sold as Contrave in the US and Mysimba in the EU and UK.
How it acts, according to the FDA labels

items.text: Naltrexone blocks opioid receptors, so opioid drugs taken while on it have little effect. The tablet label says it gives no benefit except as part of a plan to manage addiction.

Contrave's label says animal and lab studies suggest naltrexone and bupropion act on two brain areas that control eating: the hypothalamus (appetite) and the dopamine reward system. In lab studies, the pair increased firing of appetite-regulating POMC cells. The label says the exact effects that lead to weight loss are not fully understood.

research.text: For weight, naltrexone has been tested mainly with bupropion. In one trial that included naltrexone alone, each combination led to more weight loss than naltrexone alone.

research.title: Naltrexone alone, bupropion alone or both, 419 adults (Greenway et al.)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo- and single-drug-controlled, dose-finding trial in 7 US clinics
placebo; naltrexone 48 mg/day alone; bupropion SR 400 mg/day alone; or bupropion plus naltrexone 16, 32 or 48 mg/day

research.found: Compared with placebo, the combinations lowered weight by 3.5% to 4.7% more. Each combination led to more weight loss than naltrexone alone. Mild, short-lived nausea was the most common side effect. The authors called for longer studies.

src.label: Greenway FL, et al. J Clin Endocrinol Metab 2009

research.title: Naltrexone plus bupropion, 1,742 adults, 56 weeks (COR-I)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial at 34 US sites (NCT00532779)
1,742 adults aged 18 to 65 with BMI 30 to 45, or 27 to 45 with high blood fats or high blood pressure
percent weight change; share losing at least 5%

research.found: Weight fell 6.1% on naltrexone 32 mg plus bupropion, 5.0% on naltrexone 16 mg plus bupropion, and 1.3% on placebo. Half of people completed 56 weeks. Nausea affected about 3 in 10 on the combination. Depression and suicidality events did not rise. Funded by the developer, Orexigen.

research.title: The 4 COR trials in the Contrave label, 4,536 adults

facts.v: 4 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials (COR-I, COR-II, COR-BMOD, COR-Diabetes)
4,536 adults with obesity, or overweight with high blood pressure, high blood fats or type 2 diabetes; 83% women
percent weight change; share losing at least 5%

research.found: Mean weight change on Contrave vs placebo: -5.4% vs -1.3% (COR-I), -8.1% vs -4.9% with intensive behaviour therapy (COR-BMOD), -3.7% vs -1.7% in type 2 diabetes. About 45% left before week 56. 24% on Contrave and 12% on placebo stopped because of side effects.

research.title: Heart safety of naltrexone plus bupropion, 8,910 adults (LIGHT)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled non-inferiority trial at 266 US centres (NCT01601704)
8,910 overweight or obese adults at higher heart risk; mean age 61; 85% with diabetes
time to heart attack, stroke or heart death

research.found: The trial was ended after the sponsor publicly released confidential interim data. At the 50% interim look, events occurred in 2.0% on the combination and 2.3% on placebo. The authors said heart safety remains uncertain and needs a new trial.

src.label: Nissen SE, et al. JAMA 2016 (LIGHT trial)

us.text: Naltrexone is FDA approved, by prescription, for alcohol dependence and opioid dependence (Revia and generic tablets, Vivitrol injection). For weight, it is approved only in Contrave, with bupropion. Using naltrexone alone for weight is off-label. As of November 1, 2026.

items.text: Revia tablets were approved November 20, 1984 as a new molecular entity (NDA 018932, now discontinued). Generic tablets are labelled for alcohol dependence and to block opioids.
Vivitrol, a monthly injection, was approved April 13, 2006 (NDA 021897) for alcohol dependence and to prevent relapse to opioid dependence after detox.

Contrave (naltrexone and bupropion extended-release) was approved September 10, 2014 (NDA 200063) for long-term weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition. Its label says the effect on heart disease and death has not been established, and advises against combining it with other naltrexone products.
Contrave has a boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behaviours, because of its bupropion part.
naltrexone alone is not approved for weight loss. Using it that way is off-label.
naltrexone is not a controlled substance; it does not appear on DEA's list.

world.lead: Naltrexone is an approved prescription medicine in the US, Canada, the UK, the EU and Australia. The naltrexone and bupropion combination for weight is approved in all five. It is not on WADA's list.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Revia 1984; Vivitrol 2006; Contrave with bupropion 2014, weight). Prescription-only.
Approved medicine: ReVia (Teva) and generic tablets are marketed; Contrave has been marketed since 2018. Prescription-only.

after.text: European Union: in March 2025 EMA finished a review of Mysimba prompted by concerns about long-term heart risk. It found the benefits still outweigh the risks for use up to 12 months, said safety beyond that is uncertain, and required an ongoing heart outcomes study (INFORMUS) with results expected in 2028. Treatment should stop after 1 year if at least 5% weight loss is not kept, and doctors should review it every year.

after.text: Naltrexone is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or the 2027 List, and it is approved, so class S0 does not apply. Bupropion, the other part of Contrave, is on WADA's Monitoring Program but is not prohibited.

side.text: Alone, naltrexone's labels warn of liver injury, sudden opioid withdrawal in people still using opioids, and a higher risk of fatal overdose if opioids are used after stopping it. In Contrave, nausea is very common, and the bupropion part adds a boxed warning, seizures and blood pressure rises.

items.text: hepatitis and significant liver problems were seen with naltrexone in trials and after marketing.

after detox and naltrexone, people may respond to lower opioid doses than before. Using previously tolerated doses can cause life-threatening overdose; fatal overdoses have been reported after stopping treatment.
naltrexone must not be used by people taking opioid pain medicines, dependent on opioids, or in opioid withdrawal.

in an open-label study of about 570 people with alcoholism: nausea 10%, headache 7%, dizziness, nervousness and fatigue 4% each, insomnia and vomiting 3%, anxiety and sleepiness 2%. Depression and suicidal thoughts were reported in naltrexone, placebo and control groups.
Vivitrol injection-site reactions can be very severe; some needed surgery.

in trials, nausea 32.5% vs 6.7% on placebo, constipation 19.2%, headache 17.6%, vomiting 10.7%, dizziness 9.9%, insomnia 9.2% and dry mouth 8.1%. Seizures occurred in about 0.1%. Blood pressure and heart rate can rise.
Contrave has a boxed warning for suicidal thoughts and behaviours, from bupropion.
the UK MHRA warns that naltrexone and bupropion can cause dizziness or sleepiness, and rarely loss of consciousness or seizure, which can affect driving.

surprises: The LIGHT heart safety trial of naltrexone plus bupropion was stopped early after the sponsor publicly released confidential interim data, so heart safety was left uncertain; EMA in 2025 still called long-term heart safety uncertain and required a new study.
